create.name: Parmarth Niketan
create.bio:
Parmarth Niketan is a large Hindu ashram on the bank of the Ganga at Swargashram in Rishikesh, in the Himalayan foothills of northern India. It grew from the small huts that the saint Swami Shukdevanand began building there in the 1940s for meditation by the river, and today it holds several hundred guest rooms set among gardens and temples. Its president and spiritual head is Swami Chidanand Saraswati, and Sadhvi Bhagawati Saraswati, a Los Angeles-born disciple who has lived at the ashram for over twenty-five years, serves as its international director.

The day at the ashram runs through yoga and meditation classes, prayers and a fire ceremony, ending at sunset with the Ganga Aarti on its riverside ghat, which crowds gather to join and which is streamed live every evening. Through its Parmarth School of Yoga it holds residential courses and retreats on Vedanta, mantra and Vedic chanting, the Bhagavad Gita and selfless service, and every year it hosts the International Yoga Festival. Sadhviji's evening question-and-answer satsang is broadcast daily on its YouTube channel, which has carried talks, kirtan and ceremonies from the ashram since 2007.

courses.title: Vedantic Path to Self-Realisation – 2
courses.description: A nine-day residential introduction to Vedanta at the ashram, studying Shankara's Atma Bodha and the Isha Upanishad and how their teaching on the Self applies to daily life.

courses.title: Naada Yoga with Vedic Chanting II
courses.description: A follow-on course in the yoga of sacred sound, learning Vedic chants, mantras, stotras and kirtan with Sadhvi Abha Saraswati; open to those who have done the first course or another Parmarth course.

courses.title: Gita Jayanti Retreat
courses.description: A retreat around Gita Jayanti on the teaching of the Bhagavad Gita, held within the ashram's daily round of yoga, meditation and the evening aarti.

courses.title: Special New Year Spiritual Retreat
courses.description: Six days over the New Year with the resident yoga teachers, with sessions led by Swami Chidanand Saraswati and Sadhvi Bhagawati Saraswati: pranayama, asana, meditation, chanting, Himalayan walks and a New Year's morning fire ceremony.

courses.title: 7 Days of Seva: Find Yourself and Your Divinity in Service
courses.description: A nine-day retreat built around selfless service, from community meals to clean-ups and tree planting, alongside darshan, satsang, yoga, meditation and prayer at the ashram.

courses.title: International Yoga Festival
courses.description: A week-long festival held each year at the ashram, with classes from teachers of Indian lineages and international schools, exploring the eight limbs of yoga, with satsang from visiting saints.

free_resources.title: Divine Ganga Aarti and Yagna
free_resources.description: The sunset fire-and-light ceremony on the ashram's ghat, open to all every evening and streamed live, preceded by a havan half an hour before.

free_resources.title: Divine Satsang with Sadhvi Bhagawati Saraswati
free_resources.description: A live evening question-and-answer session from the ashram garden, in which Sadhviji takes questions from people in India and around the world on practice and daily life.

flags: Teachers file links Sadhvi Bhagawati Saraswati (international director, leads the daily satsang). Swami Chidanand Saraswati, the president and spiritual head, is not on Spiritpedia: possible future listing.
Possible duplicate overlap: Sadhvi Bhagawati Saraswati is listed with her own channel (@Sadhviji); the Divine Satsang videos chosen here are on the ashram's channel.
Tier from 159,000 YouTube subscribers → luminary; the ashram is also widely known (possible editorial-stature override, not raised further).
Email is the reservations inbox (on the reservations page); the general contact route is the form on parmarth.org/contact/.

Channel link on parmarth.org reads youtube.com/parmarthniketan, which yt.mjs did not resolve as given; I resolved it as youtube.com/user/ParmarthNiketan (same name, legacy user URL), giving @parmarthniketan. Owner may want to confirm.
One web search for allegations about Swami Chidanand Saraswati or Parmarth Niketan found none (results were about a different person, Swami Chaitanyananda).
Site mentions nature cure and Ayurvedic treatment facilities and a charitable clinic; not listed.
Video titles keep the channel's '|| Divine Satsang <date>' format.
